paragraphs: Cell-Guardian sells a monitoring system that watches people held in cells without physical contact or wearable devices. The buyers are correctional facilities, which the company describes as pressed by inmate welfare, liability, and staff safety demands. The record keeping is presented as protection in itself, in the form of time-stamped, auditable records covering staff and the facility.

The sensor fuses radar, thermal imaging, and computer vision to read temperature, register movement, and flag falls as they happen. Video is recorded, timestamped, and stored in the cloud. The unit itself is water-resistant and tamper-resistant, rated IP41, and mounts on a wall or ceiling. Staff reach it through a secure browser without installing extra software, and it runs over Power-over-Ethernet.

The company names suicide watch units, medical cells, and high-risk housing as the places the system goes in. Cell-Guardian was developed by Rahm Sensor Development, Inc., the team behind the VetGuardian platform. Its company page lists an address in Orlando, Florida.

quote.text: Monitor inmate conditions without physical interaction or wearable devices.
